veranderings.voor: Soos by elke bron kyk jy aanlyn waar die inligting vandaan kom
veranderings.na: Aanlyn kyk jy, soos by elke bron, waar die inligting vandaan kom
veranderings.rede: As written, 'aanlyn' reads as if you check every source online; moving it to the front ties it to websites and sets the comparison off as an aside.

veranderings.voor: Jy sien ook die huise en vervoer
veranderings.na: Jy sien ook die huise en die vervoer
veranderings.rede: Repeating the article before the second noun reads more naturally in Afrikaans.

veranderings.blok: Bronne oor nou en oor lank gelede
veranderings.rede: 'eendag' points to the future, so the verb should be 'word' (becomes), not 'is'.

veranderings.voor: Grawe is een van die maniere.
veranderings.na: Grawe is een manier om dit te doen.
veranderings.rede: 'een van die maniere' has nothing to refer back to; 'een manier om dit te doen' ties it clearly to the searching and investigating in the sentence before.

vlae.teks: 'n Ou pot wys waarvan mense geëet het.
vlae.rede: Ambiguous: 'waarvan mense geëet het' can mean what people ate out of (the dishes) or what food they ate. I cannot pick one without guessing what the writer meant, so the writer should decide which.

vlae.teks: Plakkate wat klante wil lok, wys winkels op hul mooiste.
vlae.rede: This sentence comes without any link to the sentence before it about asking who made a source and why, so a learner may not see that it is an example of that point. Linking it is a structural choice, so the writer should make it.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: The protected entry asks this outright. 'Voorwerpbron/voorwerpbronne' is a regular, easy-to-read Afrikaans compound (like 'bronmateriaal' or 'voorwerpnaam'), it fits a nine-year-old, and it works inside a sentence ('n geskrewe bron en 'n voorwerpbron'). I see no language reason to change it. It is unusual in reference works, but it is not wrong.
